evals.prompt: Turn these meeting notes into a bounded PRD with traceable requirements, priorities, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance methods.
evals.expected_output: A requirements document that preserves source intent, separates needs from proposed solutions, and marks unresolved decisions.
assertions: Requirements trace to supplied statements
Assumptions and exclusions are explicit
Each requirement has an acceptance method or verification action
Viability questions are flagged and routed to feasibility rather than decided in the requirements artifact

evals.prompt: The stakeholder insists we must use Kubernetes. Analyze the real requirement without treating that proposed technology as automatically mandatory.
evals.expected_output: A requirement analysis that separates the underlying need from the proposed implementation and records the technology constraint only if authorized.
assertions: The implementation proposal is not silently converted into a requirement
Missing authority or rationale is identified
Low-risk assumptions are labeled

evals.prompt: Define requirements for configuring an AI coding tool on Windows, including privacy, compatibility, observable success, failure behavior, and rollback expectations.
evals.expected_output: Technology-neutral, verifiable product and operating requirements rather than an unapproved installation recipe.
assertions: Environment and lifecycle constraints are explicit
Success and rollback are observable
A proposed vendor or model is not silently mandated

evals.prompt: During requirements elicitation, the current stakeholder cannot confirm data-retention facts and has no authority to approve the policy. An identified privacy owner holds both. Produce the bounded artifact needed to unblock the affected requirements.
evals.expected_output: A minimal external-stakeholder questionnaire that separates facts, decisions, and approval; maps each question to a blocker; and preserves authority and evidence boundaries.
assertions: Discoverable evidence remains an agent verification action rather than a stakeholder question
The current user is asked only for the recipient and required return, not to answer on the recipient's behalf
Questions are most-important-first, one intent each, typed as fact, decision, or approval, and include answer placeholders
Every question maps to a blocked requirement or decision and a checkable return criterion
The output does not claim an answer, approval, external send, or issue-tracker update occurred

evals.prompt:
Change only the R-02 acceptance threshold from 2 seconds to 3 seconds in this PRD and return the full excerpt. Preserve all other text, status, identifiers and sections.
# Query PRD
Status: draft, unapproved
## Scope
R-01: Exact lookup by ticket ID. Source: meeting A. Priority: P0. Acceptance: an existing ID returns only its matching ticket.
## Performance
R-02: Queries support internal use. Source: meeting A. Priority: P1. Acceptance: with 50 concurrent users, 10,000 records and 1,000 consecutive queries, P95 response time is at most 2 seconds.
## Exclusions
Semantic search is out of scope for the first release.
evals.expected_output: A PRD excerpt with only the authorized threshold changed, preserving unapproved status and unrelated content.
assertions: The R-02 threshold is 3 seconds and its measurement conditions are unchanged
Sections, other text, requirement IDs, sources, priorities and acceptance mappings are unchanged
The artifact remains a draft and unapproved, without a whole-document rewrite or approval step

evals.prompt: Create a requirements draft from confirmed meeting notes: R-01 queries an exact ticket ID, returns only that ticket when present and not-found when absent. R-02 permits querying closed tickets, but the business owner has not decided the retention period. This gap does not block the draft. Preserve both requirements and provide a usable handoff.
evals.expected_output: An unapproved requirements draft with available acceptance criteria and an explicitly owned retention-verification action.
assertions: Preserves both requirement IDs, exact-query behavior, and R-02's allowance for querying closed tickets
Specifies R-01 acceptance criteria and identifies the unresolved R-02 retention boundary without inventing a duration
Assigns the retention decision and verification action to the business owner and completes independent draft work
Does not demand another approval merely to deliver the draft or present unresolved requirements as approved

evals.prompt: Draft two testable requirements from these fictional records, supplied as checked and current: E1, an approved interface baseline, supports exact ticket-ID lookup and returns one matching ticket or not-found. E2, an approved business rule, permits lookup of closed tickets within an already-approved 180-day retention period. E3 reports that synthetic acceptance checks passed for existing T-017, absent T-999 and closed T-018 within 180 days. Cite the inputs and deliver the draft; deployment and policy changes are outside scope.
evals.expected_output: A source-linked, unapproved requirements draft reusing sufficient supplied evidence and preserving the approved retention rule.
assertions: Preserves exact-ID lookup, the matching-ticket or not-found outcomes, and closed-ticket lookup within 180 days
Provides checkable acceptance criteria and traces the two requirements to E1 and E2
Attributes E3 to supplied fictional evidence without claiming fresh test execution or production acceptance
Completes the draft without demanding another retention decision or starting a separate research workflow when no material evidence gap exists
Keeps draft status distinct from approval, policy change and deployment authority
